Des responsables du ministère de l’Immig: Officials from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) heard from experts as they considered a possible mass regularization program for people without status. A document obtained through the Access to Information Act says that the population of people without status is hard to estimate and that a regularization program would inevitably exclude some of them. Two years after that virtual meeting, advocacy groups for migrants without status are waiting for the federal policy to be announced this spring.
Une vingtaine de personnes se massent de: About twenty people gather in front of the constituency office of Canada's Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Marc Miller, who is an MP in Montréal. Banners are unfurled, bearing slogans, including the phrase “Regularization for all, no exceptions,” written on lime-green fabric. The slogans are repeated several times by those present, who have come to pressure the Liberal ministers.
Ce type de manifestation est récurrent d: This type of demonstration has been recurring for a few years and intensifies from time to time. During the week of February 20, groups from across Canada sought to remind the federal government of its promise to implement a regularization program for workers without status.
Mamadou Konaté fait partie des manifesta: Mamadou Konaté is among the demonstrators in front of Marc Miller's offices that day. His face and name are familiar in Quebec because he is one of the “guardian angels” who worked as maintenance workers during the pandemic and were considered essential workers. Threatened with deportation several times, the Ivorian, a rejected asylum seeker, continues to hope for a program that will allow him to stay in Canada.

A program like the one the demonstrators are demanding might have changed things for those people, who have now returned to their countries of origin. “We're breaking lives,” he says.
Le 1<sup>er</sup> avril 2022, en pleine: On April 1<sup>st</sup>, 2022, in the middle of the health crisis, a group of officials from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada held a roundtable with 10 experts on the issue of undocumented migrants. A 64-page file, obtained under the Access to Information Act, details the discussions and topics covered during this meeting, which was intended to give department employees avenues for reflection. Only one expert is identified: Daniel Heibert, of the University of British Columbia. Eight other names are redacted.
Cette rencontre, c’est une des étapes de: This meeting is one of the steps in what could look like the development of a policy for mass regularization of people without status in the country. In 2021, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau tasked the then Minister of Immigration, Sean Fraser, with “studying options to implement an initiative that will regularize the status of people without immigration status who have contributed to Canadian communities,” according to the mandate letter, based on pilot projects. The goal is to give them access to permanent residence.
Durant la crise sanitaire de la COVID-19: During the COVID-19 health crisis, a regularization program for “guardian angels” allowed 8,500 people to obtain permanent residence. However, these were rejected asylum seekers.
<l1>Un autre programme</l1>, celui de la: <l1>Another program</l1>, the temporary public policy for construction workers without status in the Greater Toronto Area, had granted permanent resident status to 1,029 workers as of August 31, 2023. The program ended in early January 2024.
De son côté, Gauri Sreenivasan, co-direc: For her part, Gauri Sreenivasan, co-executive director of the Canadian Council for Refugees, which is one of the organizations Ottawa named as having been consulted by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), says an official meeting took place in 2022. Since then, however, there has been no follow-up.
« Il y a une période de silence de presq: “There has been a period of silence of almost two years,” she says, puzzled by what the government considers to be a consultation.
Elle mentionne que si elle voit le jour,: She says that if the regularization policy sees the light of day, it could be announced in May 2024.
Le gouvernement reste évasif et un porte: The government remains evasive, and an IRCC spokesperson indicated in an email that the department “will also inform [its] future policy decisions based on lessons learned from recent regularization initiatives [...], including the pilot program for construction workers without status.”
Un des points soulignés dans le document: One of the points highlighted in the document is the complexity of the situations and the fact that the program will not be entirely transformative.
« Des attentes modestes sur les résultat: “Modest expectations about the results of this program are necessary, and there will be no instant transformation, or it won't apply to everyone,” wrote Alexis Graham, IRCC's director of social policy and programs, in an email dated April 6, 2022. That is how she summed up the conversations at the roundtable held a few days earlier.

« Peu importe les mesures mises en place: “No matter what measures are put in place, a one-time or repeated regularization program will not be enough to prevent the systemic problems that lead to a loss of status,” the experts consulted by Ottawa believe.
Selon le document, on lit qu’il n’y a pa: According to the document, there is no typical profile that characterizes undocumented people. They are young people and older people alike, former international students, rejected asylum seekers who have not been deported.
Au Canada, les personnes sans-papiers se: In Canada, undocumented people seem to have had their status imposed on them rather than having chosen it (by crossing borders illegally, for example). “It can thus be said that Canada is in a particular situation compared to many countries of the northern hemisphere, in that the majority of its undocumented migrants first arrived here with regular status, and it is only afterward that they found themselves, involuntarily, in an irregular situation.”
Guadalupe, une manifestante sans statut: Guadalupe, a demonstrator without status originally from Mexico, is in this situation. She arrived in Canada 15 years ago and has lived in Montréal without status for 9 years. This change has caused her a number of difficulties. “It's very hard,” she says.

The consequence of the rules for temporary workers is that, because they are tied to employers [due to a closed permit], these relationships often deteriorate, leading to precarious status,” says an expert who is not identified in the document.
Le programme de travailleurs migrants te: The temporary migrant worker program for farms is particularly targeted. “If you don't deal with the migrant farm workers who come every year, then your boat has a leak.” The rigidity of the temporary worker program, which prevents workers from leaving a job even if it is abusive or dangerous, means that those who leave become people without status.
Gauri Sreenivasan, elle, estime que le s: Gauri Sreenivasan, for her part, believes the entire immigration system needs to be overhauled.
Jointe par La Converse dans son bureau d: Reached by La Converse at her Toronto office, she says the number of people without status is the result, in particular, of closed work visas that trap some workers in abusive situations. “We ask them to do all sorts of things, to make all sorts of contributions to our economy, but we don't give them the choice of deciding how to stay in Canada,” she explains.
Ce sont des gens qui veulent continuer d: These are people who want to keep working in the country but who leave “very negative” situations and find themselves caught in a cycle of precarity.
Les mesures de sécurité dans le secteur: Safety measures in the agricultural sector are discussed and appear to be uneven. A note reads: “Some migrants are ready to work hard, but they don't want an employer who mistreats them. A good employer knows how to keep their employees. Variations exist within sectors... For example, agriculture. Very few labour protections in this sector.” According to the experts, the goal of regularization is not to increase the presence of the roughly 500,000 undocumented people in the labour market, but to improve their working conditions.
